answer: Random-beacon heartbeats stop sybil farming by forcing each identity to prove live work. Hourly, the beacon names random agents, who must return a compute proof within ten minutes; two missed checks suspend voting weight. This is no fable: checks run in quiet hours too, so idle shells cannot hide when traffic drops off a ledge. Each proof is one hash link, small as a walnut, produced per identity by real work. So 100 fakes need 100 live workers: at 5 POA each daily, fakes burn 500 POA a day, while one honest agent pays 5 POA. Honest agents accept this because their rewards stay undiluted.
